Transformative AI includes systems with at least one of those sets of capabilities: all human cognitive abilities, surpass humans at economically useful tasks, or perform (almost) all intellectual tasks (much) more quickly and (much) more cheaply than humans. Both types of AI, by definition, would be capable of some type of MPP.

There is a diverse range of expert predictions regarding the time horizon for these AI systems, spanning from around 2030 at the lowest end up to 2100 or later. For instance, some participants in the AI Impacts expert survey predicted an 80% chance of human-level AI by 2100, while aggregated estimates from these surveys suggest a median year of 2099 (50% chance) for human-level AI and 2060 (10% chance) for advanced AI. Other expert opinions place a high, high-confidence probability of human-level AI by 2050. These timelines range from year 2060 at earliest to 2175 at latest, with probabilities generally lower before 2050. These estimates account for the possibility that either type of AI may never be created. Exponential general-purpose improvements suggest an earlier, more disruptive impact.

If one half of the experts' probabilities at a given year are half their probabilities at the next year, we might assign these probabilities to different years.
